method: initialize + tools/list (anonymous, no tool called; roadmap#992)

tools.name: listAgentMemoryFiles
tools.title: List Agent Memory Files
tools.description: List the memory files stored for an agent.

tools.name: getAgentMemoryFile
tools.title: Get Agent Memory File
tools.description: Get the contents of a single memory file for an agent.

path.description: Relative path to the memory file, e.g. notes.md or context/customer.md

tools.name: listPluginCatalog
tools.title: List Plugin Catalog
tools.description: List plugins that can be referenced by name in a build's plugins array. Builds may also reference any public GitHub repository URL (https://github.com/owner/repo) as a plugin; those are not enumerated here.

tools.name: createSchedule
tools.title: Create Schedule
tools.description: Create a schedule for an agent. The schedule fires against the agent's live build. The authenticated user owns the schedule. On a team with versions, a repeating schedule for an Agent in an automation joins that automation's versions: one matching a schedule the automation already runs fires at once, and a new one is saved to the automation's draft and fires once the draft is made active (see `pending_change`).

tools.name: updateSchedule
tools.title: Update Schedule
tools.description: Update fields on an existing schedule. Only supplied fields are changed; omitted fields retain their current values. Owners may update their own schedules; team superadmins may update any schedule on agents in the current team. A schedule that belongs to an automation with versions keeps firing as its automation's active version says: a change to its timing is saved to the automation's draft and takes effect when the draft is made active (see `pending_change`), while `enabled` applies at once.

tools.name: deleteSchedule
tools.title: Delete Schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule. Owners may delete their own schedules; team superadmins may delete any schedule on agents in the current team. Deleting a schedule that belongs to an automation with versions stops it for its owner at once; the automation's versions keep the schedule for anyone else subscribed to it.

tools.name: getTeam
tools.title: Get Team
tools.description: Get a team by ID. The caller must be scoped to the requested team.

team_id.description: Duvo team UUID to operate on. API keys are pinned to a single team — omit this (it falls back to the key's team) or pass that same team; a different team is rejected. OAuth callers, who can span multiple teams, should pass the target team here.

tools.name: startNativeOAuth
tools.title: Start Native OAuth
tools.description: Start an OAuth-based connection with a native provider (Gmail, Google Sheets, Outlook, etc.). The provider path parameter is the native OAuth provider key from listIntegrations, not the integration type. Returns an authorization URL that must be opened in a browser by a human end-user; once they grant consent, Duvo creates the matching connection and redirects the browser to the optional `return_url` (or the Duvo dashboard if none is provided). Poll `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections` to detect the new connection.

provider.description: Native OAuth provider key, not the integration type. Use oauth_provider_key from listIntegrations (for example, google_gmail for integration type gmail, google_sheets for googlesheets, or microsoft_outlook for outlook); passing an integration type returns 404 "Unknown OAuth provider".

team_id.description: Duvo team UUID to operate on. API keys are pinned to a single team — omit this (it falls back to the key's team) or pass that same team; a different team is rejected. OAuth callers, who can span multiple teams, should pass the target team here.

return_url.description: Where to send the user's browser after OAuth completes.

reconnect_instance_id.description: When set, the OAuth flow will update the existing connection in place rather than creating a new one.

tools.name: authorizeMcpOAuth
tools.title: Authorize Mcp OAuth
tools.description: Start an OAuth-based connection with a remote MCP server using Dynamic Client Registration. Returns an authorization URL the user must open in a browser; once they grant consent, Duvo creates the matching connection and redirects the browser to the optional `returnUrl`.

team_id.description: Duvo team UUID to operate on. API keys are pinned to a single team — omit this (it falls back to the key's team) or pass that same team; a different team is rejected. OAuth callers, who can span multiple teams, should pass the target team here.

mcp_server_url.description: URL of the MCP server requiring OAuth.

name.description: Human-readable name to display for the connection.

custom_integration_id.description: Optional ID of a custom integration this connection should be associated with.

return_url.description: Where to send the user's browser after consent completes. Accepts an absolute URL on a domain Duvo allows, or a path relative to the Duvo frontend (e.g. `/integrations/slack`).

integration_type.description: Optional catalog integration type (e.g. `netsuite`, `asana`). When it names a known MCP OAuth catalog integration and `mcp_server_url` matches that integration's registered server, the connection is treated as a catalog connection; otherwise it requires the custom MCP servers capability.

reconnect_instance_id.description: When set, the OAuth flow will update the existing connection in place rather than creating a new one.

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client ID of a client the user registered on the authorization server themselves (e.g. a NetSuite Integration record). Takes precedence over preregistered credentials and Dynamic Client Registration. Cannot be combined with custom_integration_id. On reconnect, omit to reuse the connection's stored credentials, or provide to replace (rotate) them.

oauth_client_secret.description: Client secret for `oauth_client_id`. Omit for public clients (PKCE-only).

tools.name: checkMcpOAuth
tools.title: Check Mcp OAuth
tools.description: Probe an MCP server URL to discover whether it supports OAuth Dynamic Client Registration. Returns the authorization endpoint and required scopes when supported. Useful as a precursor to `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections/oauth/mcp/start` or `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections`. Performs no writes.

mcp_server_url.description: URL of the MCP server to probe for OAuth support.

tools.name: listPulseDashboards
tools.title: List Pulse Dashboards
tools.description: List your Duvo Pulse dashboards (live, agent-generated visualizations of your Duvo data). Ordered most recently updated first, except scope=automation, which is ordered by creation time (then id) so the whole scope can be read with the after_id cursor without a concurrent change shifting a page boundary.

limit.description: Number of results per page (1-100, default 20)

scope.description: Which dashboards to return: 'created' (yours, the default), 'team' (published to your whole team by a teammate), 'shared' (shared with you individually by a teammate), or 'automation' (owned by one of your team's automations, each carrying its automation's name).

after_id.description: Keyset cursor for reading the whole 'automation' scope: the id of the last dashboard you received; returns the page after it in (created_at, id) order. Use this instead of 'offset' when reading every page, so a dashboard created, updated or deleted between requests cannot shift a page boundary you have already passed. 400 when the id no longer names a dashboard (restart from the first page). Only valid with scope=automation.

tools.name: createPulseDashboard
tools.title: Create Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Create a new Duvo Pulse dashboard from a natural-language prompt (e.g. 'open cases by queue this week') and dispatch the first generation turn. Generation is asynchronous — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} until status is completed. The dashboard is private to you unless you set visibility to 'team', which shares it with your whole team straight away — with permission 'view' (teammates see the dashboard) or 'edit' (teammates can also iterate on it).

tools.name: getPulseDashboard
tools.title: Get Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Get a Duvo Pulse dashboard's metadata and generation status. When status is completed and html_code_present is true, fetch the rendered HTML from GET /artifacts/{artifactId}/render; the conversation is served by GET /artifacts/{artifactId}/messages.

tools.name: listPulseDataSources
tools.title: List Pulse Data Sources
tools.description: Discover queues the current editor may connect to this team-created Pulse before sampling data. Requires live dashboard edit permission and ordinary team data access. Module sources are installed with the Module. A queue ID in generated code does not grant access.

artifact_id.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

tools.name: connectPulseDataSource
tools.title: Connect Pulse Data Source
tools.description: Connect an authorized same-team queue to a team-created Pulse before sampling it. Idempotent. This bounds dashboard data access; it never grants Process membership or case-action authority. Requires both edit permission and ordinary team source access.

artifact_id.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

tools.name: disconnectPulseDataSource
tools.title: Disconnect Pulse Data Source
tools.description: Disconnect a source from a team-created dashboard. Subsequent dashboard reads and writes immediately lose access. Idempotent; does not delete the queue or cases.

artifact_id.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

tools.name: getPulseDashboardHtml
tools.title: Get Pulse Dashboard Html
tools.description: Serve a Duvo Pulse dashboard's rendered HTML document (text/html, not JSON). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML.

tools.name: getPulseDashboardPdf
tools.title: Get Pulse Dashboard Pdf
tools.description: Render a Duvo Pulse dashboard to a PDF document (application/pdf, not JSON). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML; 409 for an openui dashboard, whose substrate this exporter cannot render.

tools.name: exportPulseDashboardHtml
tools.title: Export Pulse Dashboard Html
tools.description: Render a Duvo Pulse dashboard to a self-contained static HTML snapshot (text/html, data baked in). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML; 409 for an openui dashboard, whose substrate this exporter cannot render.

tools.name: updatePulseDashboard
tools.title: Update Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Update a Duvo Pulse dashboard's settings — rename it. Only the creator can update it.

tools.name: publishPulseDashboard
tools.title: Publish Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Publish (share) a Duvo Pulse dashboard to your whole team or your whole organization, or revert it to private (creator only). When publishing, set permission to 'view' (teammates see the dashboard) or 'edit' (teammates can also iterate on it); organization-wide viewers outside the team always get view-only access.

tools.name: deletePulseDashboard
tools.title: Delete Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Delete a Duvo Pulse dashboard. Only the creator can delete it.

tools.name: duplicatePulseDashboard
tools.title: Duplicate Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Duplicate a Duvo Pulse dashboard, producing an idle clone of the current rendered dashboard. The conversation history, shares, and connections are not copied.

tools.name: sendPulseDashboardMessage
tools.title: Send Pulse Dashboard Message
tools.description: Send an instruction to iterate on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (e.g. 'make it a bar chart', 'filter to last 14 days'). The creator can always iterate; teammates can too when the Pulse is published to the team with edit access. The agent regenerates asynchronously — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} for status.

attachments.description: Attachments to hand the agent, uploaded beforehand via the upload-urls endpoint (max 5)

tools.name: createPulseDashboardAttachmentUploadUrl
tools.title: Create Pulse Dashboard Attachment Upload Url
tools.description: Issue a presigned upload URL for a file to attach to a Duvo Pulse dashboard message (e.g. an HTML dashboard to copy, or a screenshot to match). POST the file bytes to the returned upload_url as multipart form data under the field name 'file', then pass the returned attachment_id in the attachments array of POST /artifacts/{artifactId}/messages. The agent reads the file directly from its sandbox. Files live as long as the dashboard's sandbox (about 12 hours), so upload shortly before sending.

filename.description: Name of the file being attached, without any path segments

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. text/html or image/png

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes (max 25MB)

annotations.title: Create Pulse Dashboard Attachment Upload Url

tools.name: getPulseDashboardAttachmentDownloadUrl
tools.title: Get Pulse Dashboard Attachment Download Url
tools.description: Mint a short-lived presigned URL to download or preview a file attached to a Duvo Pulse dashboard message. Returns 404 once the dashboard's sandbox has expired and the file is gone (about 12 hours).

attachmentId.description: The attachment to mint a download URL for

annotations.title: Get Pulse Dashboard Attachment Download Url

tools.name: refreshPulseDashboard
tools.title: Refresh Pulse Dashboard
tools.description: Trigger an on-demand data refresh of a Duvo Pulse dashboard. The dashboard regenerates its connection-sourced values in the background — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} for status.

tools.name: stopPulseDashboardMessage
tools.title: Stop Pulse Dashboard Message
tools.description: Stop an in-flight Duvo Pulse generation turn. Requires edit access to the dashboard. Flips the dashboard to 'interrupted' and keeps any streamed-so-far reply; stopping when nothing is generating is a successful no-op.

partial_text.description: The assistant text streamed so far, kept in the conversation as the partial reply. Omit when calling from an API client without streaming state.

tools.name: listPulseDashboardConnections
tools.title: List Pulse Dashboard Connections
tools.description: List the connections (data sources) attached to a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires edit access).

tools.name: attachPulseDashboardConnection
tools.title: Attach Pulse Dashboard Connection
tools.description: Attach one of your connections (data sources) to a Duvo Pulse dashboard so the agent can use its tools (requires edit access).

tools.name: detachPulseDashboardConnection
tools.title: Detach Pulse Dashboard Connection
tools.description: Detach a connection (data source) from a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires edit access).

tools.name: answerPulseDashboardQuestion
tools.title: Answer Pulse Dashboard Question
tools.description: Answer a pending question the Duvo Pulse agent asked and resume the paused run (creator or team editors). Use the toolCallId from the dashboard's message transcript.

tools.name: listPulseDashboardMessages
tools.title: List Pulse Dashboard Messages
tools.description: List the chat transcript of a Duvo Pulse dashboard's live version (requires edit access). Returns the most recent page by default, oldest first within the page; pass `before` (a message id from a previous page) to walk back through older messages. Messages from other version branches are not included.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return (1-500, default 50).

before.description: Message id cursor: return the page of messages immediately older than this message. Omit for the most recent page.

tools.name: listPulseDashboardComments
tools.title: List Pulse Dashboard Comments
tools.description: List the comment threads on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). Each thread carries its author, the dashboard element it is pinned to, its replies oldest-first, and whether it has been marked complete.

limit.description: Maximum number of comment threads to return (1-200, default 50).

offset.description: Number of comment threads to skip, for paging.

status.description: Return only threads in this state: `open` for threads not yet marked complete, `complete` for those that are. Omit for both. `total` and `open_total` always count the whole set, so a filtered page still reports how many threads exist.

tools.name: createPulseDashboardComment
tools.title: Create Pulse Dashboard Comment
tools.description: Start a comment thread on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). Pass `element` — captured from the dashboard canvas — to pin the thread to one element; omit it for a comment on the dashboard as a whole.

tools.name: createPulseDashboardCommentReply
tools.title: Create Pulse Dashboard Comment Reply
tools.description: Reply to a comment thread on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). `commentId` must be a thread root; threads are one level deep. A thread already marked complete still accepts replies and stays complete.

tools.name: setPulseDashboardCommentResolution
tools.title: Set Pulse Dashboard Comment Resolution
tools.description: Mark a Duvo Pulse dashboard comment thread complete, or reopen it (requires view access). Pass the target state in `resolved`; the call is idempotent, and the response carries the thread with `resolved_at` and `resolved_by` set or cleared.

tools.name: deletePulseDashboardComment
tools.title: Delete Pulse Dashboard Comment
tools.description: Delete a comment or reply on a Duvo Pulse dashboard. Allowed for the comment's author and for the dashboard's creator. Deleting a thread root keeps its replies, rendered under a deleted opening comment.

tools.name: listPulseDashboardVersions
tools.title: List Pulse Dashboard Versions
tools.description: List the version history of a Duvo Pulse dashboard, newest first (requires edit access). Use the version id with the restore and version-render endpoints.

tools.name: getPulseDashboardVersionHtml
tools.title: Get Pulse Dashboard Version Html
tools.description: Serve a specific version's rendered HTML document for a Duvo Pulse dashboard (text/html, requires edit access).

tools.name: restorePulseDashboardVersion
tools.title: Restore Pulse Dashboard Version
tools.description: Restore a previous version of a Duvo Pulse dashboard, making it live again (requires edit access). Non-destructive — it moves the head pointer to the chosen version.

tools.name: createSandbox
tools.title: Create Sandbox
tools.description: Create a new sandbox for file uploads. The returned sandbox_id can be passed to POST /v2/teams/:team_id/runs to stage data for a run.

tools.name: createSandboxUploadUrl
tools.title: Create Sandbox Upload Url
tools.description: Get a presigned URL for uploading a file into a sandbox. Use for files larger than 10MB; smaller files can be uploaded directly via POST /v2/sandboxes/:sandbox_id/files.

path.description: Path where the file will be uploaded (e.g. /workspace/data.csv)

tools.name: listSandboxFiles
tools.title: List Sandbox Files
tools.description: List files in a sandbox directory.

path.description: Directory to list files from (defaults to /workspace)

tools.name: uploadSandboxFile
tools.title: Upload Sandbox File
tools.description: Upload a file directly to the sandbox. Maximum file size is 10MB. For larger files, use POST /v2/sandboxes/:sandbox_id/upload-urls.

tools.name: getRunEvaluation
tools.title: Get Run Evaluation
tools.description: Get the latest evaluation analysis for a specific agent run (Run).

tools.name: getEvalScores
tools.title: Get Eval Scores
tools.description: Aggregate evaluation counts and flag distribution for an Assignment's Jobs since the given timestamp.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only Jobs evaluated after this are counted

scope.description: When 'custom', only counts Jobs scored against the target revision's custom rubrics, and only `custom__*` rubric flags. Defaults to 'all' (platform + custom rubrics).

revision_id.description: Target a specific Assignment revision instead of the live revision. Only honoured when scope='custom' — non-custom scopes aggregate across all revisions. Defaults to the live revision when omitted.

tools.name: getEvalRubrics
tools.title: Get Eval Rubrics
tools.description: List the evaluation rubrics a Run is scored against: the platform default rubrics plus the Agent-specific rubrics for a build. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target the revision a specific Run ran against.

build_id.description: Return rubrics for this specific build (the revision a Run ran against). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

tools.name: createEvalRubric
tools.title: Create Eval Rubric
tools.description: Add one Agent-specific evaluation rubric to a build. A build may hold at most 5 custom rubrics by default (25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled); this fails with 409 once the build's ceiling is reached, and the error message states it. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target a specific revision.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

build_id.description: Add the rubric to this build (revision). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

tools.name: replaceEvalRubrics
tools.title: Replace Eval Rubrics
tools.description: Replace a build's entire Agent-specific evaluation rubric set in one call (at most 5 rubrics by default, 25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled). Existing custom rubrics are removed and the supplied list becomes the new set; pass an empty array to clear them. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target a specific revision.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

rubrics.description: The complete custom rubric set for the build. Replaces every existing custom rubric; pass an empty array to clear them.

build_id.description: Replace the custom rubrics on this build (revision). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

tools.name: updateEvalRubric
tools.title: Update Eval Rubric
tools.description: Edit a single Agent-specific evaluation rubric's title and/or description. The edit produces a NEW rubric (with a new id and slug) so previously scored Runs stay attributed to the original criterion; the response contains the new rubric.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

tools.name: deleteEvalRubric
tools.title: Delete Eval Rubric
tools.description: Remove a single Agent-specific evaluation rubric. Future Runs on the build are no longer scored against it.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

tools.name: listAgentSchedules
tools.title: List Agent Schedules
tools.description: List the schedules you own on an agent. Returns only your own schedules, whoever you are. Callers with an elevated team role can read every member's schedules on the agent, including who created each one, via `GET /agents/{agent_id}/schedules/all`.

tools.name: listAllAgentSchedules
tools.title: List All Agent Schedules
tools.description: List every team member's schedules on an agent, including who created each one. Requires an elevated team role; callers without one receive 403 and should use `GET /agents/{agent_id}/schedules`, which returns only the schedules they own.

tools.name: listAgentCaseTriggers
tools.title: List Agent Case Triggers
tools.description: List the case triggers configured for an agent. Each trigger automatically dispatches the agent to run cases added to a queue.

tools.name: previewAgentCaseTriggerConflicts
tools.title: Preview Agent Case Trigger Conflicts
tools.description: Preview which other agents would conflict with this agent's case trigger if it pointed at the given queue. Does not modify the trigger.

case_queue_id.description: The queue to check for conflicts against

tools.name: getAgentCaseTrigger
tools.title: Get Agent Case Trigger
tools.description: Retrieve a single case trigger by id.

tools.name: createAgentCaseTrigger
tools.title: Create Agent Case Trigger
tools.description: Create a case trigger for an agent. An agent may have at most one case trigger; this returns 409 if one already exists.

case_queue_id.description: Queue whose new cases should trigger this agent

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Disabled triggers do not dispatch runs.

concurrency.description: Concurrency cap for the target queue. The cap is queue-wide, so this affects every Agent working the queue, not just this trigger. Only 1 (run cases one at a time) or null (reset the whole queue's cap to the platform default) can be set here; higher caps are configured per-queue via PATCH /v2/admin/case-queues/{queueId}/concurrency. Omit to leave the queue's current cap unchanged.

tools.name: updateAgentCaseTrigger
tools.title: Update Agent Case Trigger
tools.description: Update fields on a case trigger. Only the trigger creator or a builder/admin can disable an enabled trigger or change its queue, and only a builder/admin can change queue concurrency.

case_queue_id.description: Queue whose new cases should trigger this agent

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Disabled triggers do not dispatch runs.

concurrency.description: Concurrency cap for the trigger's queue. The cap is queue-wide, so this affects every Agent working the queue, not just this trigger. Only 1 (run cases one at a time) or null (reset the whole queue's cap to the platform default) can be set here; higher caps are configured per-queue via PATCH /v2/admin/case-queues/{queueId}/concurrency. Omit to leave the current value unchanged.

tools.name: deleteAgentCaseTrigger
tools.title: Delete Agent Case Trigger
tools.description: Delete a case trigger. Only the trigger creator or a builder/admin can delete it.

tools.name: listAgentTriggers
tools.title: List Agent Triggers
tools.description: List the trigger definitions the authenticated user owns on an agent (Agent in the Duvo UI). Triggers start a Run automatically when an external event fires (e.g. an email arrives or a Linear issue is created).

tools.name: upsertAgentTrigger
tools.title: Upsert Agent Trigger
tools.description: Create or update the authenticated user's trigger for an integration on an agent. The integration must already be connected to the agent (its OAuth connection set up in the Duvo dashboard). Set `enabled: false` to pause a trigger without deleting it. An agent holds one trigger per integration for a user, so a save with a different `trigger_type` replaces the existing one — except when that trigger is an @mention trigger, which is managed from the agent's mention setting and answers 409 (`mention_trigger_protected`) here. @mention triggers are best managed from that setting throughout: this route leaves an existing one's `filter_config` untouched, and refuses to create a `teams_mention` trigger without a `filter_config.tenantId` (400, `mention_trigger_workspace_required`) — a Slack mention trigger has no equivalent field to supply.

integration_slug.description: Integration slug the trigger fires for (e.g. `gmail`, `outlook`, `linear-native`, `google-drive`).

trigger_type.description: Trigger type within the integration (e.g. `email_received`). Discover valid values via the trigger types endpoint. Integrations that enumerate their trigger types (Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Google Sheets) reject anything else with 400 (`trigger_type_unsupported`), except a save that pauses a trigger already carrying that type.

filter_config.description: Integration-specific filter config (e.g. sender/subject filters). Shape comes from the integration's filter schema. Replaces the trigger's current config, so send the whole object — except on an @mention trigger, whose config is managed from the agent's mention setting and is left as it is.

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Defaults to true.

tools.name: deleteAgentTrigger
tools.title: Delete Agent Trigger
tools.description: Permanently delete one of your own event triggers on an agent. The agent stops starting Runs for that event and the trigger's filter config is lost. To keep the trigger but stop it firing, upsert it with `enabled: false` instead.

tools.name: listAgentTriggerTypes
tools.title: List Agent Trigger Types
tools.description: List the trigger types available for an agent, grouped by integration. Use the returned `integration_slug` and `trigger_type` values when creating a trigger.

tools.name: createAgentSlackTrigger
tools.title: Create Slack Channel Trigger
tools.description: Create a Slack channel trigger on an agent (Agent in the Duvo UI): the agent starts a Run whenever a matching message is posted in the channel. An agent can carry one trigger per channel, so call this once per channel. The Slack workspace must be installed for the team AND bound to the agent's live build first (see the Slack bound-workspaces endpoint) — otherwise this returns 400.

trigger_type.description: Trigger type. Only `slack_channel_message` (a message posted in a Slack channel) is supported here.

slack_team_id.description: Slack workspace (team) ID the channel belongs to, e.g. `T0123ABCD`. Defaults to the team's default installed workspace. Discover the workspaces an agent can use with the bound-workspaces endpoint.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID to watch, e.g. `C0123ABCD`.

channel_name.description: Slack channel name shown in Duvo, without the leading `#`, e.g. `support-inbox`.

oneOf.description: Fire on every message posted in the channel.

values.description: Case-insensitive keywords; a message fires the trigger when it contains any of them. Duplicates are deduplicated.

oneOf.description: Fire only on messages containing one of the keywords.

match_rule.description: Which channel messages fire the trigger: `{"kind":"all"}` for every message, or `{"kind":"contains","values":["invoice"]}` to match keywords.

is_private.description: Whether the channel is private. Defaults to false. Private channels require the Duvo Slack app to be invited to the channel.

integration_instance_id.description: Specific bound Slack connection to run the trigger off. Omit to use your own connection, or pass one returned by the bound-workspaces endpoint.

tools.name: listAgentSlackTriggers
tools.title: List Slack Channel Triggers
tools.description: List the Slack channel triggers you own on an agent (Agent in the Duvo UI), oldest first. Each trigger's `filter_config` carries the watched `channelId`, `channelName`, Slack `workspaceId`, and `matchRule`. Capped at 100 triggers per agent.

tools.name: updateSlackTrigger
tools.title: Update Slack Channel Trigger
tools.description: Update a Slack channel trigger you own — repoint it at another channel, change which messages match, or pause and resume it with `enabled`. Only the supplied fields change. Resuming a paused trigger requires the Slack connection it runs off to still be available on the agent; changing the channel resets the trigger's seen-message state.

trigger_id.description: The Slack channel trigger's unique identifier

tools.name: reorderConfigSections

orderedAreaIds.description: Every area folder in the sibling group, exactly once, in the order you want them displayed left-to-right. Read the current siblings first (getClarityProcessTree); a partial list is rejected with 400.

parentId.description: The parent area whose folder children are being reordered. Omit or pass null to reorder the top-level areas.

tools.name: assignClarityLandscapeNodeTeam
tools.title: Assign Clarity Landscape Node Team
tools.description: Set the owning team of a process in the process landscape (organization admin+). On a proposed process this accepts the proposal and creates the real process for that team; on an existing process it moves the process, its captures and its brief to another team.

nodeId.description: The process node whose owning team changes.

teamId.description: The team that owns the process from now on. A process always belongs to a team, so null is rejected.

intent.description: Pass "accept-proposal" when the node is expected to still be a proposed process; the call then fails if someone already accepted it, instead of silently moving a real process.

tools.name: createClarityProcessNode
tools.title: Create Clarity Process Node
tools.description: File an existing Clarity process into an area of the process landscape (team builder or organization admin+). Use this for a process that already exists but sits in Unsorted; use proposeClarityLandscapeProcess to create a brand-new one.

processId.description: An existing Clarity process to file into the landscape. Unsorted processes are listed as `unlinkedProcesses` by getClarityProcessLandscape.

parentId.description: The area folder the process is filed under.

tools.name: proposeClarityLandscapeProcess
tools.title: Propose Clarity Landscape Process
tools.description: Create a manual process in the organization's Process Landscape, either as an unassigned proposal or atomically assigned to an eligible team.

description.description: One short paragraph (1-3 sentences) saying why this process belongs in the landscape. Use only what you saw in the captures. Say what the process is (don't just repeat the name), show proof it really happens, and name where you heard it - be as specific as the captures allow, like "a warehouse lead said so in their interview" or "it came up in two returns recordings". Use only facts from the captures: never make up sources, people, dates, quotes, or numbers, and don't stretch what was said. If you have no real proof the process happens, don't propose it.

materializationMode.description: Use "proposal" to record a process the organization plausibly needs, owned by `teamId` for review, WITHOUT creating a real process record. `teamId` is then required. Chat-scoped discovery agents may use proposal mode for their pinned team; direct human and API callers require Manager-or-above authority for that team. A proposal is idempotent: an equivalent live proposal under the same parent is returned untouched rather than duplicated. Defaults to "auto", which materializes a real process when `teamId` is set — except in a landscape-onboarding chat, which may only propose, and so defaults to "proposal".

tools.description: Get the v2 read model for a clarity process: the process row (with operational fields like generation_error, generation_progress, generation_started_at, generation_last_activity_at, custom_prompt), its captures, and the lightweight version arrays for both snapshot tabs. The full payload of any specific snapshot is fetched lazily via the unified per-snapshot detail endpoint (`GET .../snapshots/:kind/:id`); this read model deliberately doesn't carry it so the response stays small.

captures.description: Capture payload mode. `full` (default) embeds each capture's transcript content. `lite` omits `transcript`/`videoTranscript` (returned as null) and relies on the `hasTranscript`/`hasVideoTranscript` flags; fetch content on demand via `GET .../captures/:capture_id`.

tools.name: postprocessClaritySnapshot
tools.title: Postprocess Clarity Snapshot
tools.description: Re-run postprocessing agents on an existing v2 clarity snapshot. Targets either the current-process snapshot or the automation proposal snapshot, identified by id in the body. Flips the process status to `generating` and returns 202 immediately; agents run asynchronously and flip the status back to `review` once they settle.

tools.name: listClarityStepFrames
tools.title: List Clarity Step Frames
tools.description: Return one representative screenshare frame for each current-process step. Explicit frame evidence wins. Otherwise, a timestamped screenshare transcript source selects the closest persisted frame at or after that timestamp, with the closest earlier frame as fallback. Pass `window` (1-5) to also receive that many neighbouring frames on each side as candidates, for recovering when the selected frame does not show the step. attribution.description: Human-readable source label identifying who or what the evidence comes from. Examples: "Anna (sales interview)", "Onboarding SOP §3.2", "Slack #ops 2024-06-12"

excerpt.description: Verbatim supporting text quoted from the capture, document, or transcript. Example: "We always wait for finance to sign off before sending the invoice."

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id for this source. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

locator.description: Durable in-capture location for the excerpt. Missing means legacy free-text source; unresolved means a structured citation was attempted but could not be resolved.

messageIndex.description: Zero-based index into the capture transcript message array. This is the durable key; timestampMs is only supplemental.

timestampMs.description: Optional epoch-millisecond timestamp for the transcript message when the capture supplied one.

startOffset.description: Zero-based character offset into the stored capture text.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

pageNumber.description: Optional one-based PDF page number when the stored capture has page metadata.

startLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text starts on pageNumber.

endLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text ends on pageNumber.

elementId.description: BPMN XML element id within an uploaded .bpmn document.

elementType.description: Optional BPMN element type as parsed from the XML, for example "bpmn:UserTask" or "bpmn:ExclusiveGateway".

name.description: Optional BPMN element name as parsed from the XML. The element id is the durable key.

timestampMs.description: Epoch-millisecond frame timestamp matching a screenshare frame filename.

sourceConfidence.description: Confidence in this individual source citation. "high" = direct quote at the locator, "medium" = strong nearby evidence, "low" = weak or inferred support.

resolutionStatus.description: Resolution status for the structured source link. Legacy sources may omit this field.

condition.description: Decision criteria evaluated at this gateway. BPMN requires this on every branching gateway. Existing rows persisted with null/empty values parse as "unknown" via a read-side preprocess; producers should write a real condition string going forward.

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

proposal.description: What the new capture should include in order to resolve the gap — concrete actions, screens, or decisions the user should walk through. Optional: omit when no specific proposal can be inferred. Example: "Walk through reviewing one invoice in NetSuite end-to-end while narrating each field you check."

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

proposal.description: What the new capture should include in order to resolve the gap — concrete actions, screens, or decisions the user should walk through. Optional: omit when no specific proposal can be inferred. Example: "Walk through reviewing one invoice in NetSuite end-to-end while narrating each field you check."

readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

swot.description: SWOT analysis produced by the swot-analysis postprocessing agent. `undefined` = agent has not yet run; `null` = agent ran and produced no analysis.

strengths.description: Internal advantages of the current process — capabilities, resources, or design choices that work in its favour today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Bartenders know regulars by name, which keeps service personal during peak hours."

weaknesses.description: Internal limitations of the current process — gaps, inefficiencies, or fragile assumptions visible in how it runs today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Manual pour times balloon during rushes because there is only one tap."

opportunities.description: External openings the current process could exploit — adjacent automations, scale effects, or unmet needs surfaced by the captures. Example: "POS data could feed dynamic pricing for slow hours."

threats.description: External risks that could degrade the current process — regulatory, operational, technological, or human factors visible in the captures. Example: "New ID-check legislation will require staff to interrupt every order."

summary.description: One short paragraph (3-5 sentences) describing the captured process at a glance. Surfaced at the top of the current-process tab so reviewers can orient themselves before scanning the steps. Example: "Customers order beer at the bar; the bartender greets them, picks an option matching their preference, pours and garnishes the glass, then rings the order through the POS before serving."

projectedImpact.description: Answer-first, MECE-structured business case. 4-8 sentences of prose + one markdown assumptions table. Null when team context is insufficient to produce any quantitative or qualitative assessment.

lanes.description: Role lanes of the process map, each defined once. Absent on snapshots written before lanes existed; the read model derives them from each step's role.

id.description: Stable identifier for the lane, referenced by each step's laneId. Example: "lane-1"

name.description: The role, team, or system this lane stands for, as the reader sees it in the lane header. Example: "Finance Analyst"

limit.description: Number of agents per page (1-100, default 20)

tools.name: listOrgRuns
tools.title: List Org Runs
tools.description: List runs across every team in an organization, filtered by status, agent, team, source, evaluation issues and time. Intended for external monitoring: one call covers the whole org instead of one per team. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role, and an API key scoped to all teams you can access — a key pinned to a single team is rejected, because this endpoint spans every team in the organization.

limit.description: Number of runs per page (1-500, default 20). The cap is higher than the team runs endpoint's because this route serves bulk export: at 100 requests a minute per key, page size is what bounds how fast a month of runs can be pulled.

cursor.description: Resume after the run a previous page ended on: pass the `next_cursor` that page returned, with the same filters and sort_order. Runs created or resolved in between cannot shift a boundary you have already passed, so a sweep sees every run exactly once, and a sweep that started under the default 7-day window keeps that window on every page. This list has no offset parameter: skipping rows costs the database every skipped row, and a run created between two requests shifts every later offset by one, so an offset sweep can repeat or miss a run. 400 when the value is not a cursor this endpoint issued.

status.description: Filter to runs with this status. `needs_attention` is the monitoring status: runs that are waiting on a human or failed, plus runs whose latest evaluation flagged a critical issue — a run can finish as `completed` and still have accomplished nothing.

team_id.description: Filter to runs on this team

agent_id.description: Filter to runs for this agent

source.description: Filter to runs created from this source (e.g. api, scheduling)

has_issues.description: Filter on the run's latest successful evaluation: true returns only runs it flagged, false only runs it did not. Only the latest evaluation counts — an older flag does not match — and a run whose latest evaluation errored, or that has none, counts as unflagged. Omit to return both.

issue_severity.description: Only runs whose latest successful evaluation has at least one failing rubric at this severity (critical | medium | low). Implies has_issues.

created_after.description: Return runs created at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Every run has a creation time, so this is the window that returns all runs in a period whatever state they reached — unlike the started and completed windows below, which exclude runs that never started and runs still in flight respectively. When the request carries no lower time bound (`created_after`, `started_after`, `completed_after` or `since`), this defaults to 7 days ago and `default_window_applied` is true in the response: an organization's run history is unbounded, and a monitor wants what is recent. An upper bound alone keeps the default floor. Pass any lower bound to replace it.

created_before.description: Return runs created before this ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive). Pair with `created_after` for a period. A closed creation window is also the stable one to paginate: results are ordered by creation time, so runs arriving mid-sweep cannot shift a closed window's pages.

started_after.description: Return runs that started at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Runs that never started are excluded. Pair with `started_before` to bound a stuck-run query to a window — without a lower bound, `status=running` also counts every run left running months ago.

started_before.description: Return runs that started before this ISO-8601 timestamp. Combine with status=running to find stuck runs — `since`/`until` filter on completion, so they never match a run that is still going.

completed_after.description: Return runs completed at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Runs that have not completed are excluded, including every stuck one — reach for `started_after`/`started_before` to bound those. Alias of `since`; pass one or the other, not both.

completed_before.description: Return runs completed before this ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive). Runs that have not completed are excluded. Alias of `until`; pass one or the other, not both.

since.description: Alias of `completed_after`, kept because it is the name the public team runs endpoint ships. Prefer `completed_after`: this endpoint carries a creation and a start window too, and only the column-named pair says which one this is.

until.description: Alias of `completed_before`, kept because it is the name the public team runs endpoint ships. Prefer `completed_before`.

count_only.description: Skip row selection and enrichment. The normal list response shape is returned with an empty row array and the matching total.

include_total.description: Return `total`, the count of every matching run ignoring pagination. Off by default: counting walks every match where the page stops at `limit`, so on a large organization it costs orders of magnitude more than the rows themselves. Ask for it when you are driving a pager, not when you are polling. Implied by `count_only`.

name.description: A human-readable name for the Case schema (1–100 characters).

schema.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 subset. The root must have type "object"; every object schema, including nested objects, must set additionalProperties to false or the request fails with 400 "Object schemas must set additionalProperties to false". Allowed types: object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null. Allowed keywords: $schema, $defs, $ref, type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, description, format, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems. Allowed formats: date, date-time, email, uuid. Property names must match /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$/, and every array needs items. Schemas are limited to 65,536 bytes, 16 nested levels, and 256 declared or expanded fields; case JSON payloads are limited to 8 MiB and 10,000 items per array. Minimal valid example: {"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{}}.

tools.name: setCaseJsonDataFields
tools.title: Set Case Json Data Fields
tools.description: Set one or more fields of a typed case's structured `json_data` payload in one atomic write, leaving every other field as stored. Prefer this over `PATCH /cases/{case_id}` with a full `json_data` object when changing some fields: the write reads and locks the latest payload in the database, so a concurrent edit to another field, or to another item of the same array, is preserved. Each `set` entry names a `path`, a JSONPath declared in the queue's current Case schema, and the `value` to store there. A path is dotted object fields (`$.invoice.amount`) with optional array indices in brackets (`$.lines[0]` for a whole item, `$.lines[0].amount` for one field of it). An index must name an item that already exists; an out-of-range index or a non-array parent is refused, and a write never adds or removes items. A `value` can be any JSON value, including an object for an object field. Paths must be distinct, and no path may sit inside another in the same request (`$.lines` beside `$.lines[0]`, or `$.lines[0]` beside `$.lines[0].amount`). An index names a position, so when the array can change between your read and your write, add `expect` entries that pin the item, such as its id field (`$.lines[0].id`): if any stored value differs, nothing is written and the response is a 409. The resulting payload is validated against the queue's current Case schema and the case is re-pinned to that schema version; if any entry is refused, nothing is written. A case without a structured payload yet must be given one with `PATCH /cases/{case_id}` first. Returns the updated case with its event history and approval batches.

tools.description: List runs for the current team. Supports filtering by agent, user, queue, status, etc. Messages, evaluation data, and queue metadata are included where available. Set count_only=true to skip Run row selection and enrichment. The normal response shape is returned with data: [] and the matching total. cursor.description: Resume after the run a previous page ended on: pass the `next_cursor` that page returned, with the same filters and sort_order. Unlike offset, a cursor page does not re-read the runs before it, so a sweep does not slow down as it goes deeper; send `include_total=false` on the first page to skip the full count too. Runs created in between cannot shift a boundary already passed, so pages do not repeat or skip runs the way offset pages do. A run created or completed while a sweep is in progress can still be missed by that sweep, so to export runs continuously, poll with `since` and a short overlap and deduplicate on run id. Cannot be combined with `offset`. 400 when the value is not a valid runs cursor.

include_total.description: Whether to return `total`, the count of every matching run. Counting walks every match, so it costs far more than the page itself on a large team. tools.name: getNotificationFeed

Each item is either an individual notification or a notification batch (a per-agent group of job_issue/eval_issue/job_done/schedule_issue notifications). Filter with type, unread, and either severity (exact match) or minSeverity (threshold; the two are mutually exclusive); paginate with limit/cursor. minSeverity.description: Only return individual notifications at or above this urgency, and batches with at least one live member at or above it.
